assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Catalyst
items.clue: Speeds up a reaction without being used up.

items.label: Transition elements
items.clue: The metals in the central block of the periodic table.

items.label: Positive ion
items.clue: An ion formed when a metal atom loses one or more electrons from its outer shell.

items.label: Negative ion
items.clue: An ion formed when a non-metal atom gains one or more electrons into its outer shell.

questions.stem: Boiling points in Group 0 are helium -269 C, neon -246 C, argon -186 C. Predict the boiling point of krypton.

options.text: Below -269 C, continuing past helium at the top
About -153 C, carrying the rise further down
About -230 C, falling below argon down the group
About -246 C, the same value as neon shows

questions.explanation: Boiling points increase down Group 0, so krypton, below argon, must boil at a higher temperature than -186 C.

questions.stem: Lithium reacts steadily with water, sodium melts into a ball and potassium bursts into flame. Predict how caesium behaves.

options.text: Less vigorously than lithium, being the heaviest metal here
About the same as potassium, as both are in Group 1
Even more vigorously than potassium, reacting explosively
Steadily, because its outer electron is held tightly

questions.explanation: Reactivity increases down Group 1, so caesium, well below potassium, reacts more violently still.

questions.stem: Potassium and nickel are each added to a separate beaker of cold water. What would you see?

options.text: Both metals fizz gently, but the nickel fizzes much more slowly
Neither metal reacts, because unreactive metals like nickel show no change
Potassium fizzes and melts; the nickel does not change
The nickel fizzes strongly while the potassium slowly darkens

questions.explanation: Potassium reacts vigorously with cold water, releasing hydrogen and melting from the heat given out, while nickel shows no visible reaction.

questions.stem: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes slowly. When manganese(IV) oxide is added, oxygen is given off quickly. What is the manganese(IV) oxide doing?

options.text: It is used up in the reaction, so more must be added each time
It speeds up the reaction and is not itself used up
It raises the total volume of oxygen that can be given off
It reacts with the peroxide to release the oxygen

questions.explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide is a catalyst, one of the uses of transition metal compounds that the specification names.

questions.stem: Why does the reactivity of the Group 1 metals increase going down the group?

options.text: Atoms lower down have many more electrons to give away
Atoms lower down have more protons pulling on the shell
Atoms lower down need to gain fewer electrons
The outer electron is further out, so easily lost

questions.explanation: Going down the group the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so the attraction is weaker and it is lost more easily.

questions.stem: Freshly cut sodium and freshly polished copper are both left out in air. What happens to their shiny surfaces?

options.text: The copper stays shiny for ever, because it never reacts with oxygen
The sodium stays shiny, while the copper dulls in a few seconds
Both dull at the same rate, since both of them react with oxygen
The sodium dulls within seconds; the copper only dulls slowly over months

questions.explanation: A cut surface of sodium is coated with oxide almost at once, whereas copper reacts with oxygen very slowly unless it is heated strongly.

questions.stem: Sodium and iron are each heated in chlorine gas. Which statement about these two reactions is correct?

options.text: Sodium reacts violently, while iron reacts less readily to give FeCl3
Iron reacts far more violently, because it is the harder, stronger metal
Only sodium reacts, as transition metals never react with halogens
Both react at the same rate, because chlorine is very reactive

questions.explanation: Group 1 metals react vigorously with halogens; hot iron reacts less readily, forming iron(III) chloride, 2Fe + 3Cl2 gives 2FeCl3.

questions.stem: Element X melts at 1495 degrees C, has a density of 8.9 g/cm3 and shows no reaction with cold water. Which element is X most likely to be?

options.text: Sodium, because metals such as sodium melt at above 1000 degrees C
Lithium, because all metals are dense and sink in water
Cobalt, because those values are typical of a transition metal
Calcium, because it reacts only slowly with the cold water in a beaker

questions.explanation: Cobalt melts at 1495 degrees C and has a density of 8.9 g/cm3; a high melting point, high density and no reaction with cold water are the transition metal pattern.

questions.stem: Sodium can be cut with a knife, but chromium is used for tools and hard-wearing plating. What does this show?

options.text: Chromium is harder, so it is also the more reactive of the two
Transition elements are hard and strong, while Group 1 metals are soft
Sodium is too soft to be counted as a proper metal at all
Hardness, density and melting point are really one single property

questions.explanation: This is the strength and hardness difference the specification asks students to describe, shown here by chromium against sodium.
